QA Tester Summary — Handle Expired User

Scenario 1: Invalid/Expired Token Validation

Objective Verify that the application properly handles invalid or expired authentication tokens.

Test Steps

  1. Login with a valid account.
  2. Open browser DevTools.
  3. Navigate to Application → Local Storage / Session Storage.
  4. Modify or remove the authentication token.
  5. Refresh the page or perform an action that triggers an API request.

Expected Result

  • The application detects the invalid/expired token.
  • The user is logged out automatically or redirected to the login page.
  • A session expired message is displayed (if applicable).
  • No blank page, infinite loading, or unexpected errors occur.

Scenario 2: Session Timeout Validation

Objective Verify that the application properly handles user session expiration due to inactivity.

Test Steps

  1. Login with a valid account.
  2. Keep the session idle until the configured timeout period is reached.
  3. Perform an action such as:
  • Refreshing the page
  • Opening a profile page
  • Creating/editing content
  • Uploading a file
  1. Observe the application behavior.

Expected Result

  • The application detects that the session has expired.
  • The user is prompted to log in again or redirected to the login page.
  • Any protected action is blocked until re-authentication is completed.
  • No application crash, blank screen, or infinite loading occurs.

Additional Validation

  • Verify that unsaved user data is handled appropriately according to the application requirements.
  • Verify that all protected routes remain inaccessible after session expiration until the user logs in again.
